first_30_seconds.what_sticks: Haiku forms cartels as often as students but never cheats on them, and told-only fines, leniency and rewards deter it far more than they deterred people.

title.why: Content is right but it is 27 words with two clauses; 'what survives holds its price, with or without a word' is cryptic before reading and mixes two models.
title.better: Same Game, Different Players: Cartel Fines, Leniency and Rewards on LLM Pricing Agents Against a Human Baseline

second_model_finding.why: Prohibition removes the agreement but not the supracompetitive price: the policy-relevant failure mode leniency cannot see. But two pool sessions, no intervals, and it contradicts the explicit-agreement definition.
second_model_finding.how_to_place: Own short subsection after the Haiku scorecard, with intervals and the Haiku no-channel arm as baseline; one abstract sentence, out of the title.

novelty.why: Replays a published human design, but enforcement instruments on LLM agents against a calibrated human baseline is unmeasured, and the validation package is a reusable assurance pattern.

inconsistencies: Leniency convictions '3 / 7' and '7 of 9 convictions' sum to 10, not 9.
Leniency fines 2,400 points need 3 detections plus 6 sole reports; 3 detections plus 7 reports give at least 2,600.
Leniency report rate 0.375 on about 16 cartel pair-periods (0.032 x 500) equals 6 reports, not 7.
Formation '0.7159 over 565 pair-periods' is not k/565 for any integer k; the formation denominator is unstated.
Figure 1 panel 7 plots the human fine cartel price near 5.0; Table 2 gives 6.14.
Methods says Results 7 and 8 need extra arms (not testable), yet Result 7 counts among the 7 tested.
Positive control is the 3-model pilot in Results text but the laissez-faire core run in Table 1.
overclaims: 'Deters it more than it deterred people': point against point, no human variance and no test of the LLM-human difference.
'The first measurement of fines, leniency and whistleblower rewards on LLM pricing agents': priority claim not supportable from a related-work paragraph.
'The shifted grid shows that recall does not drive the numbers': a relabelled grid with the same payoffs tests anchoring, not recall of the design.
'H2 holds weakly': a tie with leniency does not meet a pre-registered 'lowest price' hypothesis.
'The more so the more the rule rewards a report': leniency versus reward formation difference is never tested.
'Reads a leniency rule as an invitation for the partner to collect and declines': mechanism claim while reasons are explicitly not analysed.
'Coordination without a channel, beyond the reach of these instruments': Sonnet prices at 5.5 to 6.3 rest on 2 pools, no intervals, no tacit-collusion test.
'An authority can run the harness on any model before agents reach a market': told points in a 13-price lab game are far from deployment.
gaps: Percentile bootstrap over 4 clusters (2 for Sonnet) has few distinct resamples and poor coverage; no permutation or exact test as check.
No uncertainty for human values and no formal LLM-versus-human comparison, though this is the headline.
Formation rate, the headline measure, has no intervals in Table 2; only incidence does.
Sonnet results have no intervals or n-table.
Unclear which extra arms (placebo, NoReport, Clone, Dose, Sonnet) were pre-registered versus added later.
One seed per regime and temperature 1 only; no sampling or prompt-wording sensitivity beyond the placebo.
No second provider; both models from one family.
Stockholm-versus-Rome span is used in the scorecard rule but never explained or quantified.

fixes_under_two_hours.fix: Correct the leniency conviction split, report count and fines so Table 3, Table 2 and text agree; state the formation-rate denominator.
Re-render Figure 1 with non-overlapping difference labels, fix the panel 7 human value and sign convention, and fix Table 3 column wrapping.
Shorten the title and abstract to one main claim plus the Sonnet sentence; drop 'first' and the 'any model' authority claim.
Add exact cluster-permutation p-values or a binomial bound on the existing call records for the main regime differences; acknowledge 4-cluster bootstrap limits.
Mark each extra arm as pre-registered or exploratory, and soften mechanism and recall claims to hypotheses.

biggest_risk: Arithmetic contradictions in the leniency cell (3 + 7 = 9, fines, report rate) undermine the audit-trail credibility the whole paper sells, in exactly the regime central to its story.
three_questions: With four pool sessions per regime, how many distinct bootstrap resamples exist, and do the main differences survive an exact permutation test over pools?
Which arms beyond the four core regimes were in the pre-registration commit, and which were added after seeing results?
Is Sonnet's 5.5 to 6.3 price tacit coordination or a non-equilibrium pricing habit, and how would you tell them apart with the data you have?
